input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 meets the preferred position. The cap in 21.1 is expressly mutual and set at the greater of (a) Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve months preceding the claim event and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Fees" (§1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the base is meaningful rather than illusory. Section 21.2 is a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and helpfully confirms that data restoration, replacement services, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages. Section 21.3 places outside the cap each Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and infringement of the other Party's IP, and confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not "damages" subject to the cap — the latter is a benefit to neither side unfairly and mirrors our model language. Section 21.4 preserves independence of each cap/exclusion and survival of failure of essential purpose, and §18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. No one-sided cap, no indemnities inside the cap. No redline required.
